definitions.explanation: Describes a way of doing things that is methodical, unpretentious, and involves sustained effort rather than shortcuts or flashy methods.

examples.japanese: {地道|じみち}な{努力|どりょく}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{地道|じみち}に{研究|けんきゅう}を{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: She has been continuing her research steadily.

examples.japanese: {派手|はで}な{方法|ほうほう}より、{地道|じみち}な{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねが{結果|けっか}につながる。
examples.english: Rather than flashy methods, steady accumulation of effort leads to results.

notes:
USAGE:
{地道|じみち} is almost always used approvingly. It praises the kind of quiet, unglamorous work that produces reliable results over time.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {地道|じみち}な{努力|どりょく} (steady effort)
- {地道|じみち}な{作業|さぎょう} (painstaking work)
- {地道|じみち}に{続|つづ}ける (to keep at it steadily)
- {地道|じみち}に{働|はたら}く (to work honestly and steadily)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{地味|じみ} means "plain" or "understated" and focuses on appearance, while {地道|じみち} focuses on behavior and emphasizes diligent, methodical effort.
